title: Grok Build and OpenCode CLIs are actually installed on this dev machine
trigger: Deciding whether a Grok Build or OpenCode integration check can be run directly versus deferred as "manual verification, not available in this environment."
behavior_delta: Both `grok` (Grok Build, confirmed v1.0.25 here) and `opencode` (confirmed v1.16.2 here) are real, working CLIs on this machine -- `which grok` / `which opencode` both resolve. Useful subcommands confirmed working: `grok inspect` (lists discovered instructions/skills/hooks/MCP servers for the current project), `grok plugin validate <path>` (validates a plugin manifest, reports discovered components including auto-discovered skills/ and .mcp.json), and `opencode debug startup` (loads configured plugins, including a local file:// path in the `plugin` array, and reports whether startup completed without an import-time crash). Prefer running these directly over assuming a harness integration can only get a manual, unverified check.

why: Discovered 2026-09-19 while executing docs/plans/2026-09-19-harness-native-install-plan.md Tasks 2 and 4, which had planned for `grok inspect` / a live OpenCode session as manual, likely-unavailable steps -- both tools turned out to be present and gave real signal (grok plugin validate . passed; opencode debug startup completed clean).
